title: Context receipt: what reached the model, what changed on the way, what was omitted, and why generation stopped
description: Built by clozn.runs.context_receipt.build_context_receipt() and stored on every run's `context_receipt` field (feature 06). This is the FIRST schema-governed version of that field -- runs recorded before 2026-07-27 carry an informal, pre-seam shape (top-level 'schema': 'clozn.context_receipt.v1', note the underscore and the different key name) that predates clozn/schemas/ and was never validated against any schema; those documents are read by clozn.runs.context_receipt.describe() via shape detection, never migrated in place, and never validated against this file. 'delivered' and 'assembled' are metadata-only segment arrays (source type/label/order/byte count/hash/reason) -- they deliberately do NOT carry message content; full content lives on the run's own 'messages'/'assembled_messages'/'final_prompt' fields, governed by the run-level redact/delete lifecycle (clozn.runs.mutations), not by this artifact. 'template_fingerprint' is inherited from clozn.run-identity.v1's own field, which fingerprints template AND tokenizer rendering behavior TOGETHER -- it cannot isolate one from the other, which is why 'tokenizer_conflated_with_template' rides alongside it instead of a separate (and equally unable to isolate) tokenizer_fingerprint field.

segment_reason.description: Controlled omission/transformation reason codes. Several are defined for forward compatibility but have no live detection path in clozn today: clozn is a raw OpenAI/Ollama-compatible relay with no attachment/RAG/document-chunk concept and no server-side history trimming (overlong prompts are rejected outright, never silently trimmed -- see clozn.runs.context_receipt's OVERLONG_POLICY), so context_budget/history_policy/attachment_limit/deduplicated/tool_result_pruned/system_message_merged never fire from clozn's own code today. Only template_transformed (every request is rendered through the chat template) is currently emitted unconditionally.

segment.description: One user-visible unit (v1: one chat message) tracked from delivery through rendering. Metadata only -- no content field by design; see the top-level description.

segment_id.description: seg_ + first 16 hex chars of sha256(role + "\n" + content), assigned once at the delivered boundary and carried through unchanged -- never recomputed from content at a later stage. Content-derived (not run- or position-scoped) so the same logical turn recurring across two different runs gets the same id, which is what a cross-run comparison (feature 10) needs. A disambiguating _N suffix is appended for the Nth repeat of an identical (role, content) pair within one run's delivered list.

source_label.description: Explicit client label when supplied through clozn_sources; otherwise the message role.

client_source_id.description: Optional stable client identity supplied explicitly at the request boundary. Unique within a request; never inferred.

included.description: Did this segment survive from delivered into assembled.

applied_correction.description: F5: one clozn.correction.v1 that was in effect for this run, per clozn.runs.corrections.resolve_corrections. Metadata only -- content_hash, never the correction's `content` text -- matching this schema's own top-level convention of never duplicating full text into receipt segments; the correction's own store (clozn.runs.corrections) is the content authority. This entry is the acceptance-criterion surface: a correction that shaped this run's delivered context and is not listed here would be exactly the invisible-personalization failure mode the 2026-07-27 memory-card removal was meant to end.

correction_conflict.description: F5: a same-type correction conflict that was surfaced while resolving this run's scope context, whether or not precedence produced a winner. Never omitted just because a winner was found -- see clozn.correction-resolution.v1's own description.

tokenizer_conflated_with_template.description: true whenever template_fingerprint is present: it fingerprints template AND tokenizer rendering behavior jointly and cannot attribute a change to either alone. Present as an explicit caveat rather than a separate, equally-unable-to-isolate tokenizer_fingerprint field (feature 05 independently flagged the same limitation).

bytes.description: Exact UTF-8 byte count at the inference boundary.

tokens.description: Exact worker-reported rendered prompt token count.

content_available.description: Whether this receipt's survived block still contains the exact rendered text under its privacy tier.

estimated.description: true if token_count came from a non-exact source. Native-engine runs report exact counts (omit this key -> exact); Torch lab adapters that cannot report an exact count must mark true rather than silently claiming exactness.

special_tokens.description: Not populated in v1 -- no capture point exists for which special tokens the template inserted. Omitted (never an empty-list guess) until one does.

reason_raw.description: The raw backend value the normalized reason was derived from (e.g. the engine's own 'eos'/'length'/'steps_exhausted', or a free-text error string), preserved verbatim alongside the controlled code.

source.description: Capture layer that supplied the raw reason, for example substrate, worker_event, or fallback.

privacy.description: The receipt-privacy tier active when this document was built (clozn.runs.receipt_privacy). Governs how much of THIS artifact's own duplicated content was retained -- independent of the run-level redact/delete lifecycle that governs run['messages'] etc.

applied_corrections.description: F5 (Teach Once): every scoped correction that was in effect when this run's context was assembled, per clozn.runs.corrections.resolve_corrections. Absent (never an empty-list guess) on any run recorded before this field existed, and on any run where no caller passed resolved corrections into clozn.runs.store.record -- an absent key means 'no correction evidence was computed for this run', not 'zero corrections applied'. An empty list means corrections WERE resolved and none matched this run's declared scope.

correction_conflicts.description: F5: same-type correction conflicts surfaced while resolving this run's scope context, including ones precedence already resolved. Present only alongside applied_corrections; omitted (not emptied) when corrections were never resolved for this run.
